title: BASS-II  Sample 147 (B1)  vs  Sample 148 (B3)

groups.label: Starting conditions — set before / at ignition

fields.plain: The fuel: a thin cast-PMMA (acrylic) film.
fields.note: Matrix label text differs ('100 micron pmma film' vs '100 micron film') but the material is the same. TM prints the formula 'C2H8O2', which is chemically invalid (a typo), so no formula is stated.

fields.plain: How thick the fuel film is. Thinner films burn differently from thick slabs.
Width of the fuel sample across the duct.
The ventilation air flows against the direction the flame spreads (ignited at the downstream end).
A perforated inlet plate that limits the flow range. 2 = most restriction / lowest flow range.
Forced-air (fan) flow speed measured in the duct. This is the condition that was varied between the two runs.
fields.uncertainty: The air display has a slow (~1 min) response, so instantaneous values carry uncertainty; matrix and overlay are kept separate.

fields.plain: Fan voltage setting (displayed as volts ×10) that drives the ventilation flow.
fields.uncertainty: For B1 the matrix value (62) and the overlay reading (61) differ by 1 unit — an unresolved discrepancy not explained in the sources. For B3 they agree (47).

groups.label: Observations & outcomes — recorded during / after the burn

groups.label: Recording metadata — not physical experimental conditions

fields.plain: Uncalibrated radiometer amplifier setting. Affects the displayed intensity scale only — it is an instrument setting, not a condition of the fire.
How many still photographs were captured. This is a recording choice — NOT a physical experimental condition, and NOT a verified burn duration (no per-frame burn timing is documented).
Actual test date (same GMT day 050). The video overlay shows 02/20 because the on-board clock is +1 day.
Length of the downloaded video clip. This is a recording length, not the physical burn duration.
Only a nominal series length (~95 mm) is given; the exact per-test length is not recorded.
Only a series range is documented, not the value for each specific run.
No documented per-frame burn timing or burn-duration value exists for either run.

comparison_limitations: This is a two-run comparison, not a controlled single-variable experiment. The ventilation flow differs AND so do several starting readings (initial CO₂/CO) and the specimen (147 vs 148). Any difference in the observed outcomes therefore cannot be attributed to the flow change alone — the data here does not establish cause and effect.
No continuous sensor time-series exists for either run — only single before/after O₂/CO₂/CO readings. Burn durations are not documented.
Video playback time is NOT sensor time. The two clips are independent recordings with no documented cross-synchronization; the optional link control aligns playback position only.
Temperature is not measured and must not be inferred from flame colour in either video.
The air display has a slow (~1 min) response, so the 5 vs 2 cm/s values carry uncertainty.
